text:
Microsoft Rumored to Be Killing Day One Games on Xbox Game Pass - IGN Daily Fix
In today's Daily Fix:
A rumored leak of new changes coming to Xbox Game Pass has the internet speculating on the future of the service. The biggest change reportedly coming is the loss of Day One games on the service, across all tiers. There will also be the introduction of a cheaper ad-supported tier, but online play, cloud streaming, and family accounts will all be extra add-ons. In other news, the CEO of Bulkhead, the developers of Wardogs, has defended development crunch by saying it's more of a 'balancing act,' by giving developers room to step back when things get too intense. The issue of crunch has plagued game development for decades as games, especially multi-million-dollar AAA games fall behind in development. And finally, Resident Evil direct Zach Cregger has just the actress in mind if he ever needs to cast for RE Village's Lady Dimitrescu.

text:
Wildwood - Official Final Trailer (2026) Peyton Elizabeth, Carey Mulligan, Mahershala Ali
Check out the final trailer for Wildwood, an upcoming new stop-motion fantasy film from LAIKA. Wildwood features a voice cast led by Peyton Elizabeth Lee as Prue McKeel and Jacob Tremblay as Curtis Mehlberg, alongside Academy Award nominee Carey Mulligan (Shame), Academy Award winner Mahershala Ali (Moonlight), Academy Award nominee and Emmy Award winner Angela Bassett (Black Panther: Wakanda Forever), Awkwafina (Crazy Rich Asians), Jake Johnson (Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse), Charlie Day (The Super Mario Galaxy Movie), Amandla Stenberg (Bodies Bodies Bodies), Jemaine Clement (Avatar: Fire and Ash), Maya Erskine (Mr. & Mrs. Smith), Tantoo Cardinal (Killers of the Flower Moon), Tom Waits (Seven Psychopaths) and Academy Award nominee Richard E. Grant (Can You Ever Forgive Me?).

After her baby brother is abducted by a murder of crows, headstrong teenager Prue McKeel (Peyton Elizabeth Lee) launches a desperate rescue mission into the Impassable Wilderness — an enchanted forest hidden just beyond Portland, Oregon. Joined by her hapless but loyal classmate Curtis Mehlberg (Jacob Tremblay), Prue navigates a world of talking animals, bandits, and powerful figures driven by grief and ambition. As the pair is drawn into a conflict threatening the balance of the forest itself, Prue must find a way to save her brother while confronting forces that could determine Wildwood’s future. 

Wildwood is inspired by the novel written by Colin Meloy and illustrated by Carson Ellis.

Directed and produced by Travis Knight (Masters of the Universe, Kubo and the Two Strings) and written by Chris Butler (Masters of the Universe, ParaNorman), Wildwood opens in US theaters on October 23, 2026.

text:
This PHYSINT What People Want, Sony
When Xbox snatched Hideo Kojima’s PHYSINT out from under Sony’s nose, it felt less like a standard corporate pivot and more like WCW poaching Hulk Hogan at the onset of the Monday Night Wars. Snagging the auteur behind Metal Gear Solid, the very franchise that established PlayStation's reputation for prestige storytellingm, is a massive PR flex loaded with symbolism, proving Microsoft is eager to play the aggressive underdog. But as wrestling history proves, signing the biggest icon in the business doesn't guarantee a long-term win if internal hubris and ballooning budgets take over the show.

This video breaks down the full story behind Hideo Kojima's PHYSINT moving to Xbox, Sony's surprising cancellation of Metal Gear Solid's spiritual successor, and what it means for the future of PlayStation and Xbox. With new Xbox CEO Asha Sharma securing Kojima Productions’ upcoming action-espionage game alongside OD, Microsoft is attempting a massive reset of its exclusive lineup. With Xbox looking ascendant, and Sony’s controversial shift away from single-player narrative games and the fallout from live-service missteps like Concord, are the two platform holders going to swap places soon?

Checck out The Trinca Perspective playlist for more of Jim Trinca's industry takes and other nonsense!
